summary.text: Timothy Bennett, who goes by Tim and is a Republican, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the U.S. House seat in Colorado's 7th District to Brittany Pettersen.
His campaign describes him as a retired U.S. Army Lieutenant Colonel and Ranger who sits on a school board.
He said he ran on lowering costs, supporting law enforcement, and restoring accountability in government.

paragraphs.text: Bennett's campaign website describes him as a retired Army Lieutenant Colonel and Ranger with nearly 30 years of military service. It says he has lived in Colorado since 1973 and is a single father of two, a son, Nicklaus, and a daughter, Ashleigh.
A GoodParty.org profile, built from public records and not claimed by the candidate, lists him as a Lewis-Palmer District 38 School Board member (District 1) with a term running 2026 to 2029.
Bennett advanced from the June 30, 2026 Republican primary for the 7th District as the only candidate on the ballot, with 58,806 votes.

His campaign website said he believed Congress should lower costs, support law enforcement, strengthen American energy, defend jobs, improve health care affordability, and restore accountability to government.
He received 36.1% of the vote to Brittany Pettersen's 60.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
